macro_blurb: Energy markets dominate today's tape as oil prices fell 7% after President Trump said US-Iran talks are "proceeding nicely," a move likely to weigh on European and US energy sectors while easing inflation concerns for both the ECB and the Fed. However, Iran and the US simultaneously tempered expectations of a swift end to the conflict, leaving Middle East risk premia unresolved and keeping defense and transport names sensitive to headline swings. In European autos, Ferrari unveiled its first fully electric model, a notable signal for the region's premium EV transition. Beyond that, US consumer trends show non-carbonated drinks gaining share over seltzer, a shift relevant for US beverage names.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a value-and-yield trade with a momentum kicker, not a growth screen. Across the top 10, average Momentum sits at 89.5 and Yield at 83.1, with Value at 80.8 — and Quality, tellingly, drags at 62.2. Seven of ten names carry dividend yields above 4.75%, four above 5.7%. Sector spread is wider than the factor spread: Utilities, Consumer Defensive and Healthcare each contribute two picks, with single entries from Technology, Energy, Basic Materials and Financial Services. Region mix is 8 US / 2 EU, with both European names — ENG.MC and NTGY.MC — Spanish utilities scoring 97 and 100 on Momentum. The composite range is tight (74.8–88.4), so no single name is running away from the pack.

The clearest thread runs through the high-yield, high-leverage rerating trade: ENG.MC (5.82% yield, D/E 118), NTGY.MC (7.98%, D/E 168), MO (5.74%) and KHC (6.73%) all pair top-decile yield with quality or balance-sheet question marks. With oil down 7% on the Trump-Iran headline and inflation pressure easing for the ECB and Fed, the bid for duration-like dividend payers makes sense — but the same headline directly cuts against APA, which ranks #1 on Energy Momentum (+35% in three months) on a now-weakening crude tape. HPQ sits apart: a Tech name surfacing on Value (98th percentile) and Yield (97.95), not on the AI factor driving the rest of the sector.

The outlier is CNC — no dividend, ROE of -26%, Quality in the bottom quintile, yet a 23.4% FCF yield and +36% three-month return push it into the top 10. That is a turnaround bet, not a yield-and-quality bet. The conspicuous absence: zero picks from Industrials, Consumer Cyclical, Real Estate or Communication Services out of 992 names screened — the dividend-telecom and REIT trades simply aren't clearing today's bar. Two events to watch over the next fortnight: any reversal in the US-Iran trajectory (which would flip APA and re-pressure the inflation-sensitive yield names), and further oil weakness, which would extend the same divergence.
